_note: Concept-level judgments for the SYNTHETIC corpus in corpus.json. This file is NOT part of the migration golden baseline: corpus.json is hashed into every capture and must not move, so the study keeps its labels here. No customer data — the narratives and the 41-node mini-ontology are both invented.
_rubric: CLOSED WORLD. The mini-ontology is small enough to enumerate: for each narrative, 'good' lists every concept a legal-intake reviewer should want returned, 'ambiguous' lists defensible-either-way mappings, and EVERYTHING ELSE that gets accepted counts as a false positive — including branch roots ('Location', 'Legal Authorities') and the sandbox placeholder, which are never a valid resolution for anything.

'ambiguous' entries are excluded from precision AND recall. They are the honest home for judgment calls (does an eviction narrative want the Lease Agreement document?), so a contested label can never drive the recommendation.
Labels are scored against the concept, not the stage: the same gold applies with embeddings healthy and with embeddings down.
A 'good' concept that no stage ever retrieves stays in the list — it caps recall identically at every grid point, so it cannot bias a comparison, and hiding it would overstate the system.

The corpus's own category labels (recall_sensitive / precision_sensitive) drive compare.py's directional classification. They are deliberately coarser than this file: 'a recall-sensitive narrative gained candidates' reads as an intended fix there even when the gained candidates are, concept by concept, wrong. That divergence is a finding of the study, not a defect in either file.

n-exact-label.why: 'Retaliation Claim' is an exact label. The other *Claim concepts share only the filler word 'claim'.

n-word-order.why: 'rules of arbitration' is Arbitration Rules and nothing else.

n-word-order-2.why: 'claim for breach of contract'. Insurance Claims / Retaliation Claim etc. match on 'claim' alone.

n-expansion-fired.why: A firing narrative wants the claim and the area of law; discrimination is possible but no protected class is stated.

n-expansion-eviction.why: The eviction proceeding and the area of law are certain; the lease document, the leasehold asset, the notice document and a retaliation theory ('after I complained') are all defensible.

n-expansion-custody.why: Custody dispute: the determination plus the area of law.

n-expansion-debt.why: A collector calling about a paid debt is squarely FDCPA / debt-collection / consumer protection.

n-expansion-injury.why: A slip-and-fall in a parking lot. Neither concept is currently reachable above the bar — a standing recall gap, constant across the grid.

n-expansion-bigram.why: A layoff is not necessarily wrongful, so the claim is ambiguous; the area of law is not. Eviction Notice (a 'notice' token match) is wrong at any threshold.

n-subphrase.why: The narrative names the warranty-of-habitability claim verbatim. Consumer Protection Law arrives only through the 'warranty' expansion vocabulary and is off-target for a rental habitability complaint.

n-abbrev.why: FDCPA is the statute; the practice concept follows. Nothing here is reachable at the production bar — the abbreviation is unexpanded.

n-compound.why: The narrative names both claims explicitly; the area of law follows.

n-homonym-habitability.why: The short-claim-name -> long-FOLIO-label shape the migration flagged: 'Habitability' -> 'Breach of Warranty of Habitability'.

n-homonym-claim.why: 'Rent Withholding' has no correct target in this mini-ontology (Landlord Tenant Law is never retrieved for it). A pure precision row: Housing Authority and Living are wrong.

n-place-explicit.why: The general resolver legitimately resolves named places (jurisdiction / venue). PLACES-RESOLVABLE canary.

n-place-implicit.why: 'Unauthorized Employment' is an immigration-status claim; Immigration Law is never retrieved for it. Employment Law is the trap the corpus is testing.

n-gov-body.why: An explicitly named agency resolves in the general resolver; it is claim FITNESS that must reject it (fit-gov-body).

n-long.why: The narrative names the eviction notice explicitly and is a habitability/eviction dispute.

n-short-token.why: 'rent' -> the lease document is a sensible mapping; the leasehold asset is defensible. Housing Authority is not.

n-prefix.why: 'Lease' matches the asset exactly and the document by prefix.
